interaction.speaker: Ms. Rivera
interaction.text: Welcome to Dependency Tracing Lab. Your goal: pick ONE invariant and trace it end-to-end. Check your journal for the starting point and question. Remember: failure paths are where invariants break — focus there.

interaction.content: How to submit: 1) Draw dependency graph in arrow notation: A::field -> B::fn uses it -> C::struct stores result 2) Cite file + line/function for EACH arrow 3) Return and I will verify against exact lines, not summaries.
interaction.title: Submission Format

missions.description: Read the invariant prompt at the Security Desk, then examine the starting file hint. Do not ask for summaries — read raw code.
missions.title: Start: Find Your Invariant

missions.description: Trace the specific question through the codebase. Map every read/write and upstream value. Use arrow notation and cite lines/functions for each edge.
missions.title: Build the Dependency Graph

missions.description: Return to Ms. Rivera with your graph and line citations. You will be judged on exact file+line accuracy. If wrong, you will be pointed to the disproving line to re-read.
missions.title: Submit for Verification

interaction.content:
ROUND 1 — INVARIANT: Security Check / Auth Token Flow (Failure-Path Biased)

Starting Point: The auth token / session field that gates access to protected routes — look for struct field named token, session, auth, or credentials in the main server/app entry point.

Specific Question to Answer: Trace BACKWARD: What upstream values determine whether this security check PASSES or FAILS? Include: where the value is created, every function that transforms/validates it, every place that reads it to allow/deny, and critically — all error-path and edge-case branches (malformed input, expiry, concurrent refresh, crash recovery).

Files to Start Reading: Start with the route handler / middleware that enforces the check (search for middleware, guard, authorize, verifyToken). Then follow imports backward to the token creation/validation module. Do NOT read agent summaries.

Next time you answer, include arrow graph + line citations. After verification, your errors will be logged as running notes (e.g., misses async ordering).
interaction.title: Task: Trace This Dependency

interaction.content: Reminder: Cap at ONE dependency graph per round. Bias toward failure paths: malformed tokens, expired sessions, race on refresh, missing header. Happy-path is not enough.
interaction.title: Constraints

interaction.content: Running Notes Log (across sessions) will be kept here. Current: [Session 1 — pending]. Future picks will deliberately target your weak spots: async ordering, error-path branches, concurrent access.
